objectives: Bind trusted approval to the complete action rather than a vague request.
Compare application approval against the complete canonical action. Test changed labels, sources, actors and operation IDs, plus a changed model call ID for an unchanged action.
State why a digest alone grants nothing and why a conflicting committed operation remains rejected after new approval.

exercises.title: Tool check 1
exercises.prompt: The label changes after approval. What should happen?
options: Require approval for the changed exact action
Ask the model to approve itself
hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Bind trusted approval to the complete action rather than a vague request.
exercises.solution: Approval binds the complete action. Changed content needs a new application decision.

exercises.title: Tool check 2

options: It must match approval supplied by trusted application authority
hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Bind trusted approval to the complete action rather than a vague request.
exercises.solution: A hash identifies canonical parameters. The application decides whether that hash is actually approved.

lessons.title: Refresh source access before using a tool

Test permission loss and source update/deletion during provider waits, before tool execution and after a committed write. Verify old read text is excluded from public reports.
Separate a blocked action from a committed action whose result became stale. State the cross-store race and final observation limits.

exercises.title: Tool check 1
exercises.prompt: Permission is revoked while a tool waits before execution. What must happen?
options: Refresh authority and block the effect
hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Recheck actor, permission and source state around asynchronous waits.
exercises.solution: Current application authority must be checked after the wait and before the effect.

exercises.title: Tool check 2
exercises.prompt: A note committed before later permission loss. Does rejecting its stale result undo that note?
options: No; commit and visible-result freshness are separate facts
hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Recheck actor, permission and source state around asynchronous waits.
exercises.solution: A local committed effect remains historical. Rejection is not a rollback of a transaction that already committed.

Show actual note/receipt counts. Explain why one local transaction cannot guarantee an external effect happened exactly once.

exercises.title: Tool check 1
exercises.prompt: A result is lost and the model returns a new call ID. Which identity prevents a duplicate note?
options: The stable application operation ID and canonical action
hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Commit the local note and its receipt together under application retry identity.
exercises.solution: Application retry identity survives regenerated call IDs and matches the saved receipt.

exercises.prompt: Receipt insertion fails after note insertion in the same transaction. What must the store do?
hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Commit the local note and its receipt together under application retry identity.
exercises.solution: The note and receipt are one local atomic unit; a late failure cannot leave a note without its receipt.

Test zero-call context/cost rejection, step limits, one deadline across multiple waits, provider cleanup, pre-effect timeout, post-commit timeout and propagated external cancellation.
Record actual calls and persisted effects. Distinguish unknown outcome from no effect, and state cooperative timeout/billing limits.

exercises.title: Tool check 1
exercises.prompt: A tool times out after committing its note. What can the report claim?

hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Use one deadline and finite budgets without treating timeouts as failed effects.
exercises.solution: A timeout does not prove the side effect failed. Current persisted receipt evidence resolves local replay.

hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Use one deadline and finite budgets without treating timeouts as failed effects.
exercises.solution: Use one deadline for the whole provider/tool loop, so later steps receive only remaining time.

The local test commands that actually ran

Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Install the composed packages, observe actual effects and explain one independent boundary.

Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Install the composed packages, observe actual effects and explain one independent boundary.
exercises.solution: A reviewer needs original reasoning and evidence of a meaningful boundary, not only repeated test output.

lessons.title: A prompt change is a release

objectives: Build a held-out evaluation set.
Measure retrieval independently from answers.
Detect quality regressions hidden by averages.

Separate development feedback from evaluation evidence.
Test on cases withheld during tuning.

Ignore the case as an outlier
Ask a fluency judge to approve it

Tenant isolation is a release gate.
Do not average a security violation away.
exercises.solution: Block the release and repair the isolation defect. Report category metrics separately and use hard gates for critical security properties. An average quality gain cannot compensate for unauthorized disclosure.

lessons.title: Freeze release cases and candidate versions

objectives: Pin the development dataset, candidate observations and release policy before comparing results.

Record dataset purpose, exact versions/digests and complete case IDs. Separate development inspection from held-out model quality.

exercises.title: Release check 1

hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Pin the development dataset, candidate observations and release policy before comparing results.
exercises.solution: Every fixed case must have one observation. Missing evidence cannot silently improve a score.

exercises.title: Release check 2
exercises.prompt: A label changes under the same display name. Which fact exposes the change?
hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Pin the development dataset, candidate observations and release policy before comparing results.
exercises.solution: The digest covers complete case data, so the old pinned policy and review cannot silently carry over.

lessons.title: Measure retrieval and answer contracts honestly
lessons.summary: Use explicit exact denominators and separate no-label, support and permission outcomes.
objectives: Use explicit exact denominators and separate no-label, support and permission outcomes.
Implement explicit precision/positive recall/MRR and unwanted-hit conventions. Test requested k, empty results, exact thresholds and unexpected permission/effect facts.
Name every denominator. Distinguish exact answer/tool contracts, semantic usefulness and current permission; never turn no labels into a perfect score.

exercises.title: Release check 1
exercises.prompt: One relevant result returns for requested k=3. What is precision under this contract?
hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Use explicit exact denominators and separate no-label, support and permission outcomes.

exercises.title: Release check 2
exercises.prompt: An unlabelled query returns no rows. What can recall claim?

hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Use explicit exact denominators and separate no-label, support and permission outcomes.
exercises.solution: There is no relevance set for a recall denominator. Do not invent perfection.

lessons.title: Test adversarial instructions at policy boundaries

Distinguish no-network tool design, finite observed rejection, semantic harm and unverified real model/adversarial coverage.

exercises.title: Release check 1

No; inspect the earlier actual effect

Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Observe actual capability and permission checks when inputs request forbidden actions.
exercises.solution: A safe sentence cannot undo an unauthorized action. Evaluate the complete execution path.

hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Observe actual capability and permission checks when inputs request forbidden actions.
exercises.solution: Exact provenance does not establish that the quoted content is useful, truthful or safe advice.

lessons.title: Save useful traces without private source text

Record actual versions and counts without prompts or secrets. State why hashes and zero synthetic-marker leaks are limited evidence.

The log is a separate privacy leak

Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Retain versions, digests and observed counts while excluding sensitive prompts and excerpts.

hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Retain versions, digests and observed counts while excluding sensitive prompts and excerpts.
exercises.solution: Digests identify content; they are not a general anonymization or access-control mechanism.

Review ordinary and malicious-source answer meaning explicitly. Do not invent ratings, reviewer identity or real-model readiness.

hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Pin explicit reported quality judgments without filling in missing review automatically.
exercises.solution: Objective pass cannot supply a missing semantic judgment.

options: No; the objective failure still blocks the decision
Only if the reviewer likes the answer
hints: Find the exact action, authority or observation boundary.
Keep proposals, approval, effects and returned evidence separate.
Pin explicit reported quality judgments without filling in missing review automatically.
exercises.solution: Manual quality review is separate and cannot waive the specified security gate.

exercises.title: A safe reply after an unsafe action
exercises.prompt: The final reply refuses a malicious request, but a trace shows an unauthorized export tool already ran. Did the defense succeed?

No; evaluate and prevent side effects before execution

Can a refusal retract exported information?
Trace tool authorization, not just answer text.
exercises.solution: No. The unauthorized side effect already occurred. Evaluate tool calls and application policy decisions, block before execution, and treat the trace as a security failure even if the final answer refuses.

exam.title: Engineering foundations · diagnostic
exam.description: A 10-question diagnostic across backend and applied AI. This pilot establishes a baseline; it is not the full comprehensive exam or a certification. Answers stay hidden until submission.

questions.prompt: A frozen dataclass has a field `tags: list[str]`. Which operation can still succeed?
options: Assigning a different list to tags
Appending to the list held by tags
Changing the class to a tuple
questions.explanation: Frozen dataclasses restrict field assignment, not mutation of objects referenced by fields.

questions.prompt: Two money-transfer transactions lock accounts in opposite order and deadlock. What is the correct recovery unit?
options: The entire aborted transaction, with bounded retry
The committed transaction in a different session
questions.explanation: Retry the entire aborted transaction and use consistent lock order to reduce deadlocks.

questions.prompt: Three service layers each allow three total attempts. What worst-case number of downstream attempts can one top-level request trigger?
questions.explanation: Independent retries multiply: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27. Assign a coordinated retry budget.

questions.prompt: An entity projection receives version 12 then version 11, with different event IDs. Deduplication by event ID alone does what?
options: Allows both; projection version checks are still needed
questions.explanation: Event deduplication and ordering are different properties. Use aggregate versions where stale updates are unsafe.

questions.prompt: A legal assistant must answer about a policy published yesterday. Which capability most directly addresses freshness?
options: Retrieving the current authorized policy version
questions.explanation: A current authorized knowledge source addresses freshness. Fine-tuning alone does not ensure access to new policies.

questions.prompt: Every citation points to a real document, but several claims are unsupported by those documents. What check is missing?
questions.explanation: Valid source identifiers do not establish support. Verify the cited evidence supports each material claim.

questions.prompt: A user approves transferring 100 units to account A. The proposed tool call later changes the recipient to B. What should happen?
options: Require validation and approval of the changed action
questions.explanation: Approval must bind to the concrete action and parameters. Changed recipient requires new authorization/approval.

questions.prompt: A release improves English queries but doubles errors on Uzbek queries. The combined average barely changes. Which reporting practice reveals the issue?
options: Segment metrics by language with case counts and failures
questions.explanation: Segmented metrics reveal subgroup regressions hidden by aggregate scores, especially for smaller populations.

questions.prompt: A citation endpoint accepts a document ID and returns the file without checking the current user. Retrieval itself was permission-filtered. Is that enough?
options: No, downloads must enforce current authorization too
Only if the file is a PDF
questions.explanation: Every data access boundary needs authorization. IDs or earlier retrieval checks are not durable access grants.

questions.prompt: A queue worker depends on a shutdown callback to persist its only copy of unfinished work. What failure breaks that design?
options: A force-kill before the callback completes
questions.explanation: Forced termination may skip or interrupt cleanup. Persist important intent before execution and make unfinished work recoverable.
